messages:
sec-bot: :rotating_light: Vendor alert: AuthStride reports potential exposure of OAuth refresh tokens in archived S3 logs. Affected bucket: s3://authstride-access-logs, timeframe ~2026-03-19 03:00-07:00 UTC. No direct Redwood keys mentioned.

authstride-support: Hey Redwood team — we found plaintext refresh_token values in a debug dump we accidentally archived. We have: rotated our service account creds, revoked refresh tokens issued in that window, tightened bucket ACLs, and started an object-level inventory. Sharing findings here as requested.

olivia-sec: Thanks. Olivia from Security — can you confirm whether those logs contained any IDs that map to our customer IDs or Redwood-managed client_ids? :eyes: Also confirm whether the S3 objects were encrypted with SSE-KMS or vendor-managed keys.

authstride-support: We saw some client_id values that match Redwood integrations (obfuscated partials). Objects were SSE-S3 initially; we switched to SSE-KMS yesterday but objects in the time window were not KMS-encrypted.

ryan-ops: Ryan — I'll run an access audit for any GetObject events to that bucket and check for unusual IPs. Putting commands here for transparency:```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:s3:::authstride-access-logs --max-results 50
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket authstride-access-logs --query 'Contents[?LastModified>=`2026-03-19T03:00:00Z`]'```

sam-devex: Sam — from a product integration side, we should rotate any client secrets we control and mark the integration as temporarily suspended until we confirm no tokens exposed are still valid. Ryan, can you confirm whether any Redwood refresh tokens or client secrets show up in that dump?

ryan-ops: Running a grep on downloaded sample blobs now. Quick check:```grep -E "refresh_token|client_secret" sample-log-blob.txt | head -n 10``` If I find matches I'll paste masked examples. So far seeing 2 masked client_ids and one pattern that looks like a refresh token but needs correlation.

olivia-sec: If there are Redwood tokens, we need immediate containment: 1) rotate affected client secrets 2) force refresh token revocation for impacted users 3) revoke vendor service account and create temporary integration key. Also enable object-level logging in our side if we subscribe to their events.

authstride-support: Understood. We've queued a full rotate and will provide a sanitized dump for your forensics. We are also limiting access to the bucket to a small allowlist and will enable SSE-KMS for all future objects.

kate-legal: Kate from Legal — keep me posted on scope (how many end-users, whether PHI is involved). We may need to trigger notification playbooks. Please preserve chain-of-custody of the artifacts you share.

sam-devex: Noted. I'll start an internal change to suspend the integration in staging and prod if any matching tokens are found. Also want to add an RBAC follow-up: deny the 'log-dumper' role from cross-account S3 listing. That role is too permissive.

olivia-sec: Post-incident actions: - validate CloudTrail data events for that bucket were enabled - require SSE-KMS for vendor logs moving forward - add audit alert for any object ACL changes - require vendor to use SSE-KMS with a vendor-managed CMK and rotate yearly - add a contract clause for immediate notif + 24h remediation SLA.

ryan-ops: Quick update: saw 3 GetObject events from two IPs we don't recognize in the window. I've blocked those IPs at the edge and requested vendor to revoke any external keys associated. Saving logs to sec-s3 for triage.

authstride-support: We will send the sanitized sample and proof of rotations within 2 hours. We apologize — will also run a retro to prevent debug dumps being archived.

olivia-sec: Good. Forensics next steps: collect the sanitized archive, map any extracted tokens to our session store, identify exposed user subsets, and prepare notification slate if needed. Sam, coordinate the integration suspension and key rotation. Kate, hold on notifications until we have user impact numbers.

sam-devex: On it. I will post updates here as actions complete. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: Incident state changed: vendor_third_party_investigation -> containment_in_progress (incident_id: VEND-2026-03-19-01).
